note: Live Map polish: selected Stop ID searches keep the highlighted stop visible above the ETA sheet, and mobile viewport/input sizing was tightened so phone users do not need to pinch-zoom out after focusing controls.

vision.statement: An AI-powered transit assistant for Gainesville RTS riders that understands plain-language questions and guides the customer to the right answer — whether that's a real-time ETA or a scheduled departure time.
vision.cx_journey: Customer arrives at the assistant and types a question in plain language (e.g. 'When does the next 75 leave Butler Plaza?'). The assistant leads the interaction — asking clarifying questions when needed — until it can deliver the specific ETA or schedule information the rider needs.
vision.wizard_strategy: The Trip Wizard is the conversation flow prototype. It makes the decision tree explicit (intent → route → stop → direction → result) in a structured UI so the paths can be validated. Once proven, the same guided logic is translated into the chat assistant's prompting — the AI replicates the wizard's flow in natural language instead of button clicks.
vision.end_state: A single assistant interface where any RTS rider can ask a transit question in plain English (or Spanish) and get a reliable, accurate answer without needing to know stop IDs, route numbers, or schedules.

summary.goal: Deliver a stable Gainesville RTS backend with realtime bus info, schedule support, and a user-facing web assistant/dashboard.

tasks.title: P2-D: Landmark-to-stop resolution for arbitrary locations

Options: (A) Expand stop_areas.json with known Gainesville landmarks mapped to specific stop IDs — low cost, limited coverage. (B) Add Google Places / OSM geocoding call to find nearest GTFS stop to a described location — broader coverage, adds external API dependency. tasks.title: Session 20: Fix _enrich_realtime silently dead since day 1
tasks.details: Two bugs: (1) get_predictions called with wrong keyword arg prmstpid= instead of positional stop_id. (2) Response dict was iterated as keys instead of using .get('prd'). Both fixed — real-time predictions now actually applied to first leg departure times.

tasks.title: Session 20: Fix SQLite connection leaks in trip planner
tasks.details: conn.close() was not in try/finally blocks in _service_ids_for_date() and find_trips(). On any exception, connections were left open. Fixed with proper try/finally.

tasks.title: Session 20: Fix wrong service banner on future-date trip queries
tasks.details: get_active_service_label() was called with no argument, always using today's date. For future-date queries (e.g. 'arriving by Saturday 9am'), the banner showed today's service type. Fixed: pass target_date explicitly.

tasks.title: Session 20: Raise _find_direct LIMIT from 10 to 30
tasks.details: On busy routes or wide search windows, LIMIT 10 truncated results before all viable trips were seen. Raised to 30.

tasks.title: Session 20: Add tzdata to requirements.txt
tasks.details: ZoneInfo('America/New_York') requires either system timezone data or the tzdata PyPI package. Linux containers (e.g. Render) may lack system tzdata. Added tzdata to requirements.txt as explicit dependency.

tasks.title: Session 20: CRITICAL — Fix 'No routes found' on all non-Weekday service days
tasks.details: Root cause: find_nearest_stops() returned any stop present in stop_times regardless of service type. On Reduced_Service days, returned stops were Weekday-only — routing SQL filtered by service_id='Reduced_Service' and found nothing. Fix: service_ids computed first in find_trips(); find_nearest_stops() accepts optional service_ids and JOINs trips table to filter stops by active service. Both 1km and 5km fallback scans use the filter. Impacts every search on Reduced_Service, Saturday, and Sunday.

tasks.title: Add GitHub Secrets for analytics backup action
tasks.details: Add RENDER_BACKEND_URL and DASHBOARD_PIN to GitHub repository secrets so analytics-backup.yml can run.

tasks.title: Trip Planner: Sort toggle UI (Best Match / Least Walking / Fewest Transfers)
tasks.details: Client-side only — reorders rendered itinerary cards without re-querying backend. Three buttons: Best Match (default score), Least Walking (walk_to+walk_from), Fewest Transfers (transfer count).

tasks.title: Phase 7: PWA — manifest.json + service worker
tasks.details: manifest.json + sw.js + meta tags enable 'Add to Home Screen' on iOS/Android. Required before App Store wrapper.
